name: UDP Component
description: This component allows reception and transmission of data over a network using the [User Datagram Protocol (UDP)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_Datagram_Protocol). In conjunction with the [Packet Transport Component](https://esphome.io/components/packet_transport#packet-transport) it can be used to broadcast sensor data.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Addresses
config_entries.description: One or more IPv4 or IPv6 addresses to send data to. Defaults to `255.255.255.255`, the local network broadcast address. IPv6 addresses require `enable_ipv6: true` in the [Network](https://esphome.io/components/network/) component; on ESP8266 and RP2040 the `udp` component rejects them at validation. A `%` scope suffix and link-local unicast destinations (`fe80::/10`) also fail validation, because the device cannot pick an interface for them; use multicast, unique local or global addresses instead. Multicast destinations leave on the interface the `listen_address` group was joined on, or on the first IPv6 interface when there is no IPv6 group. On nRF52 with [OpenThread](https://esphome.io/components/openthread/), a `udp:` block with a destination outside the Thread mesh (a global address, or a multicast address with a scope wider than realm-local, such as `ff05::`) sends its IPv6 datagrams from the device's off-mesh routable (OMR) address. Until a Thread border router has given the device one, its IPv6 datagrams are dropped, not queued, and a warning is logged. Destinations treated as inside the mesh (unique local addresses in `fc00::/7` and multicast up to realm-local scope) in the same block are dropped too. Use two `udp:` blocks to keep the mesh traffic independent.

config_entries.label: Listen Address
config_entries.description: An IPv4 multicast or broadcast address, or an IPv6 multicast address, to listen on. A multicast address joins that group; a broadcast address, such as the default `255.255.255.255`, only listens. IPv6 multicast addresses (e.g. `ff12::6053`) have the same `enable_ipv6`, platform and `%` scope suffix requirements as IPv6 `addresses` above. With the default `listen_address` and `enable_ipv6: true`, the device also receives IPv6 unicast datagrams sent to its own address, except on ESP8266 and RP2040. **NOTE**: When set to a multicast address, the socket binds to the group address and receives only datagrams sent to that group, whichever family the group is in: IPv4 broadcast packets (`255.255.255.255`) and IPv6 unicast datagrams sent to the device's own address are no longer received. Outgoing `addresses` are unaffected.

config_entries.label: Port
config_entries.description: The destination UDP port number to use. Defaults to `18511`. Different listen and broadcast ports can be specified via a map instead of a single port number.:
